result:
I'll leave the decision with you rather than re-prompting. To summarize the state plainly:

- **Code is committed-quality and the runtime is correct** — the only unmet item is the *visual* travel of the authored slash, which is an asset-authoring limitation, not a C++ placement bug.
- The operator report at `Reports/AgentReviews/Hero1BounceVisibleCarrierFix/claude_operator_report.md` now honestly reflects this as **BLOCKED — NEEDS HUMAN DECISION** with the four options and my recommendation (re-author the asset into a travelling streak).

My recommendation remains **re-authoring `NS_Hero1AxeBounce_MeshSlash`** into a longer, travel-mapped streak — it's the only path that robustly delivers "originates at the hero and moves toward enemies" while keeping the authored system. But that's an asset-regeneration change behind the decision gate, so I need your go-ahead before touching it.

Tell me which way you want to go and I'll proceed.

questions.question: The authored Bounce slash renders as a short in-place burst at the spawn point, so it won't visibly travel hero→target no matter how I move the carrier in C++. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Re-author the asset
options.description: Modify NS_Hero1AxeBounce_MeshSlash via the commandlet into a longer streak / travel-mapped reveal. Robustly satisfies 'originates at hero, moves to enemy' but is an asset-regeneration change (gated).

options.label: Multi-burst stamp
options.description: Spawn the existing first-iteration slash at staggered points along each segment so the eye reads progression. No asset change, but more moving parts.

options.label: Diagnose the blob
options.description: Investigate whether the cyan blob at the hero is a separate owner-anchored effect masking the real carrier, then fix that. No asset change; uncertain payoff.

options.label: Accept as-is
options.description: Keep the slash forming at/near the hero each link; document that visible travel isn't achievable with the asset as authored.
